To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the global teams are more effective than the domestic teams, but only when they are led by the global leaders.

the use of global virtual teams is associated with the following: (1) higher team performance; (2) higher team member satisfaction; (3) higher team member learning; (4) higher team member motivation; (5) lower team member turnover; (6) higher team member commitment; and (7) higher team member trust.

the following factors are important for the success of global teams: (a) the team composition, (b) the cultural distance between team members and the cultural distance between the team and the host culture of the organization, (c) the team structure, (d) the team process and team leadership, and (e) the team context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to build and lead global teams.
understanding the role of culture on global teams and how culture can be used to facilitate global team performance.
understanding how the global virtual team can be a powerful tool for the development of leadership skills and competencies.

global teams are a new phenomenon and are still in the early stages of development, but they will continue to grow and develop as organizations continue to become more global in nature.
global virtual teams can be successful, but it depends on the situation, the task and the people.
global teaming is a process of bringing together individuals from different cultures and locations to accomplish a common goal.
